context: Transaction-level XRPL metadata confirms a 20M XRP receipt followed by two near-20M deposits to a Binance-labelled account. The same destination account receives numerous tagged deposits from other exchanges. A separate 10M RLUSD transfer to r39TA came from an unlabelled account; Ripple appears as the token issuer, not the sender identity.
decision: Use raw transaction Account, Destination, Amount, DestinationTag, issuer, ledger_index and AffectedNodes balance deltas to distinguish sender from token issuer.
Never infer Ripple company ownership from a Bithomp token label such as RLUSD (Ripple); verify the sending account independently.
Classify rNxp4h as a shared exchange deposit/omnibus-pattern candidate, not a proven reserve wallet, until Binance PoR or official wallet documentation confirms its role.
Record exact account-level balance sequences separately from same-unit provenance and economic-purpose hypotheses.
Treat deposits to Binance-labelled accounts as deposits only; do not infer sale, reserve acquisition or replenishment.
invariants: No merge, force-push, workflow dispatch, paper-state mutation or real-money trade.
No Ripple-company sender attribution without account-level evidence.
No reserve classification without official PoR or exchange disclosure.
Forecast remains NOT_ISSUED; no feature admission from these transfers.
